title: Docs update: Ultimate AI Connector for WebLLM v1.1.0
body:
## Release
Ultimate AI Connector for WebLLM v1.1.0 — released 2026-04-09

## Required doc updates

- [ ] `docs/addons/ultimate-ai-connector-webllm/index.mdx` — Document the new floating chat widget: what it does (any logged-in user can prompt the browser-side LLM from the front end), the admin-bar status indicator, and how to enable/disable it.
- [ ] `docs/addons/ultimate-ai-connector-webllm/index.mdx` — Document the new widget settings in the Connector panel: toggle for the chat widget, auto-prompt behaviour configuration.

## Changelog entry

```
= 1.1.0 =
Released on 2026-04-09

* New: floating chat widget with admin-bar status indicator — any logged-in user can prompt the browser-side LLM directly from the front end.
* New: SharedWorker runtime — the MLC engine now runs in a SharedWorker so multiple tabs share one GPU session instead of fighting over it.
* New: apiFetch middleware interceptor — WordPress REST requests that match the AI Client SDK pattern are transparently routed to the local WebLLM broker, no loopback HTTP round-trip needed.
* New: widget settings UI in the Connector panel for toggling the chat widget and configuring auto-prompt behaviour.
* Fix: force IndexedDB cache backend so model weight downloads survive HuggingFace xet CDN redirects that break the default Cache API path.
* Fix: skip the context_window KV-cache override for embedding models (they have no decoder and the override caused a runtime error).
* Fix: advertise the cold-start candidate model in /webllm/v1/models before the worker tab has loaded, so SDK consumers see a model immediately.
* Fix: hook WebLLM into the wpai_preferred_text_models filter so the AI Experiments feature routes to the browser engine when a model is configured.
* Improved: cache-busting, content normalisation, and hardware-reference fixes surfaced during end-to-end testing.
```

title: chore: upgrade GitHub Actions from Node.js 20 to Node.js 24
body:
## Problem

GitHub Actions is deprecating Node.js 20. Actions running on Node.js 20 will be forced to Node.js 24 starting **June 2, 2026**, and Node.js 20 will be removed from runners on **September 16, 2026**.

This repo's workflows use actions that still run on Node.js 20, producing deprecation warnings on every run.

## Required upgrades

| Current | Upgrade to |
|---------|------------|
| `actions/checkout@v4` | `actions/checkout@v6` |
| `actions/setup-node@v4` | `actions/setup-node@v6` |

`shivammathur/setup-php@v2` is already on Node 24 (v2.37.0) -- no change needed.

## How

EDIT: `.github/workflows/*.yml` -- find-and-replace the action version tags per the table above.

For `softprops/action-gh-release`, add this env var to the workflow or job level until upstream releases a Node 24 version:

```yaml
env:
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: true
```

## Verification

After merging, trigger a workflow run and confirm no Node.js 20 deprecation warnings appear in the annotations.

## References

- [GitHub blog: Deprecation of Node 20 on GitHub Actions runners](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/)

title: Screenshot audit and refresh program (master)
body:
## Summary

A repo-wide audit of every screenshot in `static/img/` and every `/img/...` reference in `docs/` revealed widespread problems:

- **147 image files** are tracked, but only **98 unique paths** are referenced from `docs/` — and many of those single paths are reused for dozens of unrelated concepts.
- **At least 32 files are byte-for-byte duplicates** of each other (same MD5 hash) saved under different names.
- **At least 4 walkthroughs** (Zapier, Stripe, PayPal, Customer account page) currently use a single screenshot as a placeholder for every step.

This issue tracks the program of work. Each focused area has its own child issue (linked below).

## Goal

Every screenshot in the docs should:

1. Show the actual UI being described.
2. Be unique per concept (no recycled placeholder).
3. Be cropped/sized to highlight the relevant control, not buried in chrome.
4. Be reasonably small (file size + image dimensions) so the docs site stays fast.

---

## Capture environment

The dev WordPress used to take new screenshots:

- URL: <http://wordpress.local:8080>
- Username: `admin`
- Password: `admin`
- Plugin: Ultimate Multisite (current `main` build) active on the network.

Open the login page at `http://wordpress.local:8080/wp-login.php`, sign in, then go to **My Sites → Network Admin → Ultimate Multisite** to reach every screen referenced in the docs.

If `wordpress.local:8080` is not reachable from your machine, ask in the issue thread for access (a staging clone can be provided).

## Capture standards

| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Browser window for screen captures | **1280 × 800** (consistent across the whole doc set) |
| Device pixel ratio | 1× (use a normal/external monitor, not a Retina-only display) |
| Theme | WordPress default admin colour scheme, no admin-bar customisations |
| Browser zoom | 100% — confirm with `Ctrl/Cmd + 0` before each shot |
| File format | PNG, 8-bit RGB, non-interlaced |
| Max longest edge | **1568 px** — anything larger gets auto-downscaled and wastes bytes |
| Min readable text height | ≥ 12 px after any cropping |
| Crop policy | Crop tightly to the panel/section being described. Do **not** capture the whole admin chrome unless the doc text refers to the sidebar / admin bar. |
| Annotations | None by default. If the doc text already describes the control, the screenshot should speak for itself. |
| File name | Keep the existing filename when replacing. For new shots, use `kebab-case-area-element.png` and place under `static/img/admin/`, `static/img/config/`, or `static/img/installation/` to match siblings. |
| Optimisation | Run `pngquant --quality=70-90 --skip-if-larger -f -o out.png in.png` (or `oxipng -o 4 in.png`) before committing. Target < 200 KB unless the screen genuinely needs more detail. |

### Recommended capture tools

- **Linux:** Flameshot (`flameshot gui`), GNOME Screenshot, or `gnome-screenshot -w` for a window.
- **macOS:** `Cmd + Shift + 4`, then space, then click the browser window. To remove window shadows: `defaults write com.apple.screencapture disable-shadow -bool true`.
- **Cross-platform:** Playwright/Chromium headed: open <http://wordpress.local:8080/wp-admin/network/admin.php?page=wp-ultimo>, resize window to 1280 × 800 via the OS or DevTools device toolbar, then capture.

For full reproducibility you can drive the capture from a tiny Playwright script (1280 × 800 viewport, deviceScaleFactor 1) — useful if you’re doing many at once. Ask in this issue if you want a starter script.

### Filename hygiene

- Never paste a screenshot with macOS’s default name `Screenshot 2026-… PM.png` into commits — rename to the target path first.
- On macOS, the AM/PM in the default filename contains a U+202F narrow no-break space which breaks many tools. Rename to ASCII before committing.

---

## Audit findings

### A. Exact byte-identical duplicates (same file content, different names)

These were verified with `md5sum`. The recycled name almost always implies a screenshot that was never actually captured.

| MD5 | Affected files | Tracking issue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `023edc1399…` | `static/img/config/product-{custom-domains,disk-space,hide-credits,plugins,post-types,reset-limitations,site-templates,themes,upgrades}.png` (9 files, all 28 236 B) | #69 |

title: Screenshot audit — replace placeholder reuse and missing captures across docs
body:
## Summary

Audit of every screenshot reference in `docs/` (English source). Findings:

- **147** image files tracked under `static/img/` (`admin/`, `config/`, `installation/`).
- **98** unique images are actually referenced from English docs.
- **48** image files are orphans (exist on disk, never referenced). Several are exactly the per-step screenshots that the docs *should* be using but are not — they need rewiring before any new captures are taken.
- **27 doc pages** reuse the same image two or more times within a single page (a single image illustrating up to 14 different UI states). This is the primary "same screenshot used several times" pattern that needs replacing.
- **28 addon pages** under `docs/addons/*/index.mdx` contain **zero** screenshots.

The full inventory is tracked across the child issues linked below. This master issue is the place for the shared capture playbook and the cross-cutting checklist.

## Worst offenders (one image used many times in one page)

Links to each child issue will be added in a follow-up comment.

---

## Screenshot capture playbook

This playbook is the single source of truth referenced by every child issue. Follow it for every screenshot you take or replace.

### 1. Local environment

The docs are written against a local WordPress Multisite that resolves at:

```
http://wordpress.local:8080
```

**Login**: navigate to `http://wordpress.local:8080/wp-login.php`, username `admin`, password `admin`.

If `wordpress.local` does not resolve, add it to `/etc/hosts`:

```
127.0.0.1   wordpress.local
```

If a local stack is not running yet, the project ships everything you need under the Multisite Ultimate test environment (use the same admin/admin credentials whichever way you spin it up — Docker, Local, Lando, valet, etc.). Open the **Network Admin** dashboard (`/wp-admin/network/`) — every Ultimate Multisite menu lives under **Network Admin → Ultimate Multisite**.

### 2. Seed data (so screenshots are not empty)

Many of the current screenshots show empty/zero state which looks unfinished in the docs. Before capturing, make sure each list has realistic but innocuous data:

- **Customers**: 6–10 with varied join dates and at least one cancelled.
- **Memberships**: at least one Active, one Trialing, one On Hold, one Cancelled, one Expired.
- **Sites**: 6–10 sites across two or three plans.
- **Products**: at least three plans (Free, Basic, Pro) and one Package/Service.
- **Domains**: two mapped custom domains, one in `Ready`, one in `Checking DNS`.
- **Payments**: a mix of `Completed`, `Pending`, `Refunded` so the list looks real.
- **Discount codes**: at least one percentage code, one fixed-amount, one expired.
- **Broadcasts**: one Email broadcast, one Notice broadcast, one Draft.
- **Webhooks**: one configured endpoint plus the default ones.
- **Events**: leave the events log running so it has recent entries.

Use names that look generic but professional. Never use real customer data. Email addresses should be `customer-N@example.com`, names from a clearly fictional list (e.g. `Jane Doe`, `Acme Designs`, `Beach Studio`).

### 3. Browser and viewport

Use a clean Chrome / Chromium / Firefox profile (incognito or a dedicated profile) with:

- **No browser extensions visible** (Grammarly, Honey, password manager toolbars, dev-tools panels).
- **Default zoom 100%**.
- **Light mode** WordPress admin colour scheme (`Users → Your Profile → Color Scheme → Default`).

Resize the browser window so the captured screenshot is no wider than necessary. Recommended viewports:

- **Settings / list / table pages**: 1280×800 (DPR 1) or 1280×900. This is wide enough to show the WP admin sidebar plus the page content without horizontal scroll, and narrow enough that the right-hand whitespace doesn't dominate the screenshot.
- **Edit forms / modals / dialog boxes**: 1024×768 is plenty; the screenshot should focus on the form, not the surrounding chrome.
- **Frontend checkout / pricing tables**: 1366×900 desktop, plus a 414×900 mobile capture if the page describes mobile behaviour.

If you need a really focused capture (e.g. a single toggle, a single button), crop tightly after taking the screenshot — don't try to do it with browser-resize alone. Aim for **400–900 pixels wide** for "inline" screenshots that illustrate one control.

### 4. Capture mechanics

Two acceptable workflows:

1. **DevTools device toolbar** (Chrome `Cmd+Shift+M` / `Ctrl+Shift+M`): set "Responsive" to the viewport above, then `⋮ → Capture screenshot`. This gives you pixel-exact output and excludes the OS chrome.
2. **OS screenshot tool with window selection**: macOS `Cmd+Shift+4` then press `Space` and click the window; Windows `Win+Shift+S`; GNOME `PrtSc → Screenshot a window`. Make sure no notification toasts are visible.

After capture:

- **Crop** to remove dead space, but keep enough context that the reader can locate the control on the screen (the immediate breadcrumb / heading / surrounding label).
- **Annotate sparingly**. If you must, use the `annotation` style already used in `static/img/installation/multisite-wizard/` (red rounded rectangles, no shadows, no arrows pointing to obvious things).
- **Strip metadata** (`exiftool -all= file.png` or equivalent) — no need to leak the capture machine.
- **Optimise** with `oxipng -o2 file.png` or `pngquant --quality=85-95 --speed 1 file.png`. Target file size **under 200 KB**, ideally under 100 KB.

### 5. File names and placement

Existing naming convention:

- `static/img/admin/<short-name>.png` — Network Admin pages and dialogs that the super admin sees (`memberships-list.png`, `customer-edit.png`, `webhooks-list.png`).
- `static/img/config/<short-name>.png` — Settings pages and product / discount / checkout editors (`settings-payments-full.png`, `discount-code-edit.png`).
- `static/img/installation/<short-name>.png` — One-time setup wizards.
- `static/img/installation/multisite-wizard/<short-name>.png` — Multisite wizard sub-flow.

Keep names hyphenated, lowercase, descriptive of the screen — not the doc that uses it. Reuse the existing names when re-capturing the same screen so docs that link them don't need editing. **Where the docs reference a generic placeholder, add new files with a more specific name** (e.g. `discount-code-edit-percentage.png`, `stripe-webhook-endpoint-url.png`).

Several files already exist on disk but no doc references them yet — see the **Rewire existing orphan screenshots** issue for the list; in many cases the right fix is "wire up the existing file" before capturing anything new.

### 6. After replacing screenshots

1. Run `npm run build` and `npm run serve` to inspect each affected page locally and confirm every image renders.
2. Re-run any image-optimisation step that CI relies on.
3. Translations under `i18n/*/` may reference English filenames — the translation pipeline picks up replaced files automatically when filenames stay the same, but new filenames must be added to the relevant translated markdown. Run `python3 fix-i18n-images.py` (already in the repo) afterwards if any image paths change.
4. Commit screenshots and the doc edits together so review is one diff.

### 7. Acceptance criteria for closing a child issue

- Every alt-text in the affected doc has a screenshot whose **content actually matches** the alt-text.
- No image appears more than once in the same page **unless** the page is genuinely re-referencing the same screen (rare; document the reason in the PR description if so).
- Each new file is under 200 KB and metadata-stripped.
- `npm run build` succeeds.
- `i18n/*/` builds pass (the CI workflow handles this).

title: Docs update: Ultimate Multisite: Captcha v1.5.0
body:
## Release
Ultimate Multisite: Captcha v1.5.0 — released 2026-05-22

## Required doc updates

- [ ] `docs/addons/ultimate-multisite-captcha/index.mdx` — document the hard-stop rate limiter, protected surfaces, HTTP 429/Retry-After behaviour, tarpit timing, and the `cap_rate_limit_tarpit_min` / `cap_rate_limit_tarpit_max` settings.
- [ ] `docs/addons/ultimate-multisite-captcha/index.mdx` — document trusted client-IP attribution, Cloudflare header trust, trusted proxy CIDR configuration, first-enable auto-detection, and mismatch admin notices.
- [ ] `docs/addons/ultimate-multisite-captcha/index.mdx` — mention the new rate-limit-specific IP bypass filter and pre-block action at a high level, linking to generated hooks docs when available.

## Changelog entry

```text
Version: 1.5.0 - Released on 2026-05-22
* New: Hard-stop rate limiter — counts every GET and POST on captcha-protected surfaces (wp-login / register / lost-password / comments, WooCommerce my-account / checkout / pay-for-order, Ultimate Multisite checkout / inline-login) and replies with HTTP 429, a `Retry-After` header, and a randomised tarpit sleep (1–5s, hard-capped at 15s).
* New: `cap_rate_limit_tarpit_min` / `cap_rate_limit_tarpit_max` settings to tune the tarpit window.
* New: `wu_cap_rate_limit_whitelist_ip` filter to exempt trusted IP ranges.
* New: `wu_cap_rate_limit_will_block` action that fires immediately before the hard-stop response is sent.
* New: Spoof-resistant client-IP detection. `Captcha_Core::get_client_ip()` (the source of truth for rate-limit bucket keys, captcha siteverify `remoteip`, and statistics IP hashes) now enforces a strict trust model: REMOTE_ADDR is the floor, `CF-Connecting-IP` is honoured only when the immediate peer is inside a current Cloudflare IP range, and `X-Forwarded-For` is honoured only when the immediate peer is in the admin-configured trusted-proxy list, with a right-to-left walk that skips trusted/CF hops before settling on the visitor IP.
* New: `cap_trust_cloudflare_headers` setting (default OFF) — opt into `CF-Connecting-IP` trust when behind Cloudflare. The plugin ships a bundled Cloudflare CIDR snapshot and refreshes it weekly via wp-cron with bundled fallback if the refresh fails.
* New: `cap_trusted_proxies` setting — textarea of CIDRs or bare IPs (one per line, `#` comments allowed) listing your own front-line proxies / load-balancers. Without this, `X-Forwarded-For` is ignored even when the rate limiter is enabled.
* New: First-enable auto-detection of likely Cloudflare / proxy posture with a one-click "Apply detected settings" admin notice. The plugin never overwrites your saved values; if subsequent traffic suggests your config no longer matches reality (e.g. Cloudflare changed CIDR ranges and your proxy CIDR is now stale), a non-dismissable mismatch notice surfaces the recommended update.
* Fixed: Invisible mode no longer silently downgrades `cap_security_level` to FAST — the admin's configured level is honoured. A new `wu_cap_server_security_level` filter is available for sites that want bespoke logic.
* Fixed: Statistics `rate_limits_triggered` counter now increments on every block, not only on the rare post-success backstop path.
* Fixed: `Captcha_Core::get_client_ip()` is now the single source of truth for visitor IP attribution across the rate limiter, captcha providers (reCAPTCHA + hCaptcha `siteverify`), and statistics — closing a spoofing vector where direct origin-server requests carrying a forged `CF-Connecting-IP` header would have been bucketed by the spoofed IP instead of the real peer.
* Fixed: WooCommerce classic checkout rate-limit gate now fires on `template_redirect` (priority 1) instead of `woocommerce_before_checkout_form`. The form-level hook never fires when the cart is empty, so flood traffic that never adds a product was bypassing the limiter entirely.
* Fixed: WooCommerce pay-for-order rate-limit gate now fires on `template_redirect` instead of `woocommerce_before_pay_action`. The latter only fires after `wp_verify_nonce('woocommerce-pay')` succeeds, which means unauth attackers (the actual threat model) never triggered the limiter.
* Fixed: WooCommerce Store API (blocks) checkout rate-limit gate now fires on `rest_pre_dispatch` instead of `woocommerce_store_api_checkout_update_order_from_request`. The latter only fires after Store API validates the cart and billing fields, so unauth bots got a 400 from the validator and never tripped the limiter.
* Fixed: Ultimate Multisite inline-login rate-limit gate now fires on `wu_ajax_nopriv_wu_inline_login` priority 1 (and the logged-in mirror) instead of `wu_before_inline_login`. The latter only fires after `check_ajax_referer('wu_checkout')` succeeds, so unauth bots without a valid wu_checkout nonce got a 403 and never tripped the limiter.
* Fixed: `Rate_Limiter::enforce()` now applies a once-per-request guard keyed by `surface|ip`, so upstream hooks that fire twice per render (notably `wu_setup_checkout` in Ultimate Multisite) no longer halve the effective rate-limit threshold.
* Fixed: Rate-limit surface gates no longer consult `Captcha_Core::is_whitelisted()` (`wu_captcha_whitelisted` filter). That filter signals "captcha already handled by another surface" and is orthogonal to flood protection — the WooCommerce integration was hooking it to skip the WordPress login captcha when a Woo nonce was present, which bled into rate counting and let Woo POSTs avoid the limiter. The rate-limit-specific `wu_cap_rate_limit_whitelist_ip` filter is the only bypass that now applies.
```

- Confirm whether `multisite-wizard/wizard-welcome.png` and `installation/wizard-welcome.png` refer to intentionally different wizard flows. Document the distinction in a comment on this issue.

```bash
git add static/img/installation/

Ref #64

Replaces byte-identical duplicate plugin-activated.png/wizard-welcome.png
```

## Release
Ultimate Multisite v2.13.0 — released 2026-06-05

## Required doc updates

- [ ] `docs/user-guide/configuration/` — document sovereign-tenant/customer-panel behavior changes, including disabled tenant-side checkout and customer-facing UI routing back to the main site where applicable.
- [ ] `docs/developer/hooks/` — no manual edit needed if regenerated, but verify the generated hook docs include the new SSO URL and domain-record extension points.
- [ ] `docs/developer/integration-guide/` — add guidance for custom tenant routing/authentication integrations using the new SSO URL and checkout-form base-domain/domain-record extension points.
- [ ] `docs/user-guide/domain-mapping/` — update domain mapping/DNS management notes for checkout-form base domains and automatic domain-record creation behavior.

## Changelog entry

```text
Version [2.13.0] - Released on 2026-06-05
- New: Added sovereign-tenant support for customer account, checkout, billing, site, invoice, template switching, and domain mapping flows so tenant networks can direct customers back to the main site for managed actions.
- New: Added renewal-credential checks for recurring memberships so gateways can disable auto-renewal when a saved billing agreement, subscription, or vault token is missing.
- New: Added HMAC-verified loopback publishing for pending site creation to make checkout-to-site provisioning more reliable on hosts where background jobs are delayed.
- New: Added developer extension points for SSO URLs, checkout-form base domains, and automatic domain-record creation.
- Fix: SSO is more reliable across mapped domains, anonymous broker visits, logout, and cross-plugin dependency conflicts.
- Fix: Pending site creation now recovers from stale publish flags and avoids leaving customers stuck on the site-creation screen.
- Fix: Domain records are no longer created for shared checkout-form base domains, and unused host-provider background jobs are skipped when no integration is active.
- Fix: Checkout, billing address, password reset, email verification, template switching, tours, and customer dashboard edge cases no longer block normal customer flows.
```

title: Use Superdav AI Service for docs translations
body:
## Goal

Route the Docusaurus documentation translation workflow through Superdav AI Service (`superdav-chat-pro`) while keeping the existing OpenAI-compatible script path, preserving existing translations, and avoiding secret leakage.

## Context

The docs repo already has the right integration shape:

- `.github/workflows/translate.yml` runs `node scripts/translate.js --concurrency 2 --commit` with `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_BASE`, and `OPENAI_MODEL` from repo secrets.
- `scripts/translate.js` supports the OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` provider via `OPENAI_API_BASE`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and `OPENAI_MODEL`.
- Superdav AI Service exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint under `/v1/chat/completions`; use `OPENAI_MODEL=superdav-chat-pro`.
- `scripts/translate.js` writes `_i18n_hash` into translated frontmatter, but the current skip path is path-only: an existing destination file is skipped before checking whether `_i18n_hash` still matches the source hash.

## Files to inspect/change

- `.github/workflows/translate.yml`
- `scripts/translate.js`
- `scripts/audit-translations.js`
- `docusaurus.config.js`
- `README.md`

## Implementation notes

- Prefer the existing OpenAI-compatible env var names rather than adding a new provider unless a concrete script need appears.
- Configure GitHub Actions for the public Superdav API base URL from the repo secret/variable layer; GitHub-hosted runners cannot use a production-local `127.0.0.1` endpoint.
- Use a docs-specific Superdav site token stored only as a GitHub secret. Do not commit, print, or log token values.
- Normalize base URLs so both `https://api.sdaiagent.com/v1` and an equivalent configured `/v1` base do not produce duplicate or missing `/v1` path segments.
- Preserve existing translations by default. Re-translate only when a destination is missing or when the stored `_i18n_hash` does not match the current English source hash. Keep `--force` as the explicit full retranslation path.
- Keep debug logging safe: it may show prompts/responses when requested, but it must never show bearer tokens or full secret-derived headers.

## Acceptance criteria

- `translate.yml` can run against Superdav using `OPENAI_API_BASE`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and `OPENAI_MODEL=superdav-chat-pro`.
- `scripts/translate.js --dry-run` reports work for missing or stale translations, not for hash-matched existing translations.
- Existing translated files are skipped only when their `_i18n_hash` matches the current source hash, unless `--force` is set.
- Stale translations with mismatched or missing `_i18n_hash` are retranslated or clearly reported as needing translation.
- `scripts/audit-translations.js` still passes for generated translations and continues to catch hallucinated, truncated, blank, orphaned, and untranslated files.
- README documents the Superdav-backed translation workflow using placeholders for secrets, not real tokens.
- No workflow logs, script output, commits, or docs expose the Superdav site token.

## Suggested verification

- `npm ci`
- `OPENAI_API_BASE=<superdav-public-v1-base> OPENAI_API_KEY=<docs-site-token> OPENAI_MODEL=superdav-chat-pro node scripts/translate.js --locales es --files <small-doc-file> --dry-run`
- After a safe smoke target is chosen by the implementer/maintainer: `OPENAI_API_BASE=<superdav-public-v1-base> OPENAI_API_KEY=<docs-site-token> OPENAI_MODEL=superdav-chat-pro node scripts/translate.js --locales es --files <small-doc-file> --concurrency 1`
- `node scripts/audit-translations.js --locales es`
- `npm run build`

## Out of scope

- Replacing the Docusaurus translation architecture.
- Bulk translating every locale in this issue unless the maintainer explicitly requests it after the Superdav path and hash-based incremental behavior are verified.

body:
## Consolidation target: #64

**Parent issue:** #64 in `Ultimate-Multisite/docs`
**Parent title:** Screenshot audit and refresh program (master)
**Parent labels:** `documentation,enhancement,help wanted,origin:worker,origin:interactive,status:available,consolidation-in-progress`

> You do **NOT** need to read #64. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #64 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "Ultimate-Multisite/docs" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` is also mandatory. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #64:**

```bash
gh issue comment 64 --repo "Ultimate-Multisite/docs" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 64 --repo "Ultimate-Multisite/docs" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 64 --repo "Ultimate-Multisite/docs" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "Ultimate-Multisite/docs" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #64 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @superdav42."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "Ultimate-Multisite/docs" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #64** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @superdav42

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Summary

A repo-wide audit of every screenshot in `static/img/` and every `/img/...` reference in `docs/` revealed widespread problems:

- **147 image files** are tracked, but only **98 unique paths** are referenced from `docs/` — and many of those single paths are reused for dozens of unrelated concepts.
- **At least 32 files are byte-for-byte duplicates** of each other (same MD5 hash) saved under different names.
- **At least 4 walkthroughs** (Zapier, Stripe, PayPal, Customer account page) currently use a single screenshot as a placeholder for every step.

This issue tracks the program of work. Each focused area has its own child issue (linked below).

## Goal

Every screenshot in the docs should:

1. Show the actual UI being described.
2. Be unique per concept (no recycled placeholder).
3. Be cropped/sized to highlight the relevant control, not buried in chrome.
4. Be reasonably small (file size + image dimensions) so the docs site stays fast.

---

## Capture environment

The dev WordPress used to take new screenshots:

- URL: <http://wordpress.local:8080>
- Username: `admin`
- Password: `admin`
- Plugin: Ultimate Multisite (current `main` build) active on the network.

Open the login page at `http://wordpress.local:8080/wp-login.php`, sign in, then go to **My Sites → Network Admin → Ultimate Multisite** to reach every screen referenced in the docs.

If `wordpress.local:8080` is not reachable from your machine, ask in the issue thread for access (a staging clone can be provided).

## Capture standards

| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Browser window for screen captures | **1280 × 800** (consistent across the whole doc set) |
| Device pixel ratio | 1× (use a normal/external monitor, not a Retina-only display) |
| Theme | WordPress default admin colour scheme, no admin-bar customisations |
| Browser zoom | 100% — confirm with `Ctrl/Cmd + 0` before each shot |
| File format | PNG, 8-bit RGB, non-interlaced |
| Max longest edge | **1568 px** — anything larger gets auto-downscaled and wastes bytes |
| Min readable text height | ≥ 12 px after any cropping |
| Crop policy | Crop tightly to the panel/section being described. Do **not** capture the whole admin chrome unless the doc text refers to the sidebar / admin bar. |
| Annotations | None by default. If the doc text already describes the control, the screenshot should speak for itself. |
| File name | Keep the existing filename when replacing. For new shots, use `kebab-case-area-element.png` and place under `static/img/admin/`, `static/img/config/`, or `static/img/installation/` to match siblings. |
| Optimisation | Run `pngquant --quality=70-90 --skip-if-larger -f -o out.png in.png` (or `oxipng -o 4 in.png`) before committing. Target < 200 KB unless the screen genuinely needs more detail. |

### Recommended capture tools

- **Linux:** Flameshot (`flameshot gui`), GNOME Screenshot, or `gnome-screenshot -w` for a window.
- **macOS:** `Cmd + Shift + 4`, then space, then click the browser window. To remove window shadows: `defaults write com.apple.screencapture disable-shadow -bool true`.
- **Cross-platform:** Playwright/Chromium headed: open <http://wordpress.local:8080/wp-admin/network/admin.php?page=wp-ultimo>, resize window to 1280 × 800 via the OS or DevTools device toolbar, then capture.

For full reproducibility you can drive the capture from a tiny Playwright script (1280 × 800 viewport, deviceScaleFactor 1) — useful if you’re doing many at once. Ask in this issue if you want a starter script.

### Filename hygiene

- Never paste a screenshot with macOS’s default name `Screenshot 2026-… PM.png` into commits — rename to the target path first.
- On macOS, the AM/PM in the default filename contains a U+202F narrow no-break space which breaks many tools. Rename to ASCII before committing.

---

## Audit findings

### A. Exact byte-identical duplicates (same file content, different names)

These were verified with `md5sum`. The recycled name almost always implies a screenshot that was never actually captured.

| MD5 | Affected files | Tracking issue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `023edc1399…` | `static/img/config/product-{custom-domains,disk-space,hide-credits,plugins,post-types,reset-limitations,site-templates,themes,upgrades}.png` (9 files, all 28 236 B) | #69 |
| `1dce0a089f…` | `static/img/admin/network-dashboard-{activity-stream,first-steps,full,news,right-now,summary}.png` + `static/img/installation/network-dashboard.png` (7 files, all 125 540 B) | #70 |
| `28184a7caf…` | `static/img/admin/settings-payments-{bottom,gateways-2,options}.png` (3 files) | #71 |
| `1c1ac4f60f…` | `static/img/config/period-selection-field-{options,settings}.png` (2 files) | #72 |
| `74f697dd4b…` | `static/img/installation/plugin-activated.png`, `static/img/installation/wizard-welcome.png` | #75 |
| `b9c1d601bb…` | `static/img/admin/um-dashboard-bottom.png`, `static/img/admin/um-dashboard-stats.png` | #76 |

**Total: 32 files that should collapse to ~10 distinct shots.**

### B. One screenshot reused for many concepts inside one doc (placeholder pattern)

| Doc file | Distinct concepts illustrated | Image used | Tracking issue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `docs/user-guide/integrations/zapier.md` | 14 (Zapier dashboard, app search, trigger picker, auth modal, UM API settings, credentials, payment_received event, test step, action setup …) | `webhooks-list.png` — wrong screen for **every** step | #65 |
| `docs/user-guide/payment-gateways/stripe.md` | 13 (UM active gateways, inline card field, Checkout redirect, API keys, Stripe Dashboard, test-data toggle, Stripe webhooks, listener URL, endpoint paste …) | `settings-payment-gateways.png` — wrong screen for most steps | #66 |
| `docs/user-guide/payment-gateways/paypal.md` | 5 (UM active gateways, API credentials, PayPal account settings, PayPal API integration, generated credentials) | `settings-payment-gateways.png` — wrong screen for the PayPal-side steps | #67 |
| `docs/user-guide/client-management/account-page.md` | 16 (account menu, account overview, plan summary, Site Limits, Billing Address, update form, change template button, switch confirmation, Add Domain, DNS instructions, change password form, Danger Zone …) | Recycled mix of `dashboard.png`, `customers-list.png`, `domains-list.png` from the **network admin** — but the doc is about the **customer-facing subsite account page**. | #68 |

### C. Cross-doc placeholder reuse (heaviest offenders)

| Image | Times referenced | Used for | Tracking issue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/img/admin/webhooks-list.png` | 35 | Mostly Zapier walkthroughs | #65, #74 |
| `/img/config/settings-payment-gateways.png` | 34 | PayPal + Stripe walkthroughs | #66, #67 |
| `/img/admin/memberships-list.png` | 17 | Memberships list, but reused for cancel / downgrade / upgrade flows where the actual screens differ | _(future)_ |
| `/img/config/checkout-form-step.png` | 16 | Re-used for every field type configuration | #72, #73 |
| `/img/config/settings-taxes.png` | 15 | VAT add-on walkthrough | _(future)_ |
| `/img/config/discount-codes-list.png` | 14 | Multiple distinct discount-code editor screens | _(future)_ |

---

## Workflow per child issue

For each linked child issue:

1. Open `wordpress.local:8080`, log in as `admin / admin`.
2. Re-create / open the screen described in the doc text.
3. Capture per the standards table above (1280×800, tight crop, < 200 KB).
4. Save to the exact path listed in the issue (overwrite existing file — keep the filename).
5. If the issue says "split into N shots", add the new filenames to `static/img/.../` and update the markdown references in the listed `docs/...` file accordingly.
6. Run `npm start`, visit the doc page, and confirm every shot renders and matches the surrounding text.
7. Commit with a message like `docs(screenshots): refresh <area> per issue #<N>` and open a PR referencing the issue.

## How this audit was done

```bash
# All tracked images
git ls-files | grep -iE '\.(png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp)$'

# Exact-duplicate detection
find static/img -type f -name '*.png' -exec md5sum {} \; | sort | uniq -d -w 32

# Reference counts per image
grep -rohE '/img/[^)" ]+\.png' docs/ | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn

# Image dimensions / file sizes
find static/img -name '*.png' -exec file {} \;
```

- **Touring the admin panel** (`touring-the-admin-panel.md`) — verify each linked screen still matches the current UI.

These can be ticketed as needed once the high-impact issues above are landed.

title: consolidated: screenshot audit and refresh program
body:
_Supersedes #64 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Run the repository-wide Screenshot Audit and Refresh Program. Every documentation screenshot must depict the UI described beside it, be unique to that concept, tightly cropped to the relevant control, readable, and optimized for the documentation site. Deliver the work through the already-filed child issues; retain this issue as the program tracker.

### Program inventory and delivery structure

- The English docs currently track 147 image files, reference 98 unique image paths, and include at least 32 byte-identical duplicate files.
- Existing focused children remain the implementation queue: #65 Zapier, #66 Stripe, #67 PayPal, #68 customer account, #69 product limitation tabs, #70 network dashboard widgets, #71 payment tabs, #72 checkout editor, #73 registration form (after #72), #74 webhooks, #75 installation wizard, #76 analytics dashboard, #77 site templates.
- The second audit added children #84 (28 addon `index.mdx` pages with no screenshots), #85 (48 unreferenced `static/img/` files; examine reusable captures before recapturing), and #86–#96 for the gap pages listed in **How**.
- Keep #64 as the historical source, but use this issue as the single current specification. Issues #78–#83 were duplicate section programs and remain superseded; do not reopen them.
- Lower-priority, not-yet-filed work: re-capture the populated-list states in `docs/user-guide/administration/touring-the-admin-panel.md` and `docs/user-guide/administration/managing-memberships.md` with seed data.

## Why

The audit found screenshots reused for unrelated concepts, including walkthroughs where one placeholder illustrates every step. This makes instructions misleading, conceals current product UI, and adds unnecessary static assets. The program replaces placeholders with accurate shots, wires in useful orphan captures before taking new ones, and keeps images fast and consistent.

## How

### Capture and asset standards

| Requirement | Standard |
| --- | --- |
| Capture viewport | 1280 × 800 at device-pixel-ratio 1 and browser zoom 100% |
| Admin appearance | Default WordPress admin colour scheme; no admin-bar customisation |
| Format | 8-bit RGB, non-interlaced PNG |
| Size | Longest edge no more than 1568 px; normally target under 200 KB |
| Readability | Text remains at least 12 px after cropping |
| Crop | Tight panel/section crop; include WordPress chrome only when the docs discuss it |
| Annotation | None unless the existing documentation requires it |
| Naming | Preserve replacement names; new captures use `kebab-case-area-element.png` under the matching `static/img/admin/`, `static/img/config/`, or `static/img/installation/` directory |
| Optimization | Run `pngquant --quality=70-90 --skip-if-larger -f -o out.png in.png` or `oxipng -o 4 in.png` before commit |

Capture against the current Ultimate Multisite main build in the authorized local WordPress environment. Use authorized credentials without recording them in commits, comments, screenshots, or issues. Standard tools include Flameshot/GNOME Screenshot, macOS Screenshot, or a headed Playwright/Chromium window configured to the capture viewport. Rename macOS screenshots to ASCII before committing; the default name can contain a narrow no-break space. Do not retain default `Screenshot … AM/PM.png` names.

### Per-child workflow

1. Re-create or open the screen described by the target documentation text.
2. Capture to the exact existing asset path, or add the narrowly named new asset path stated by the child issue.
3. For a split walkthrough, update the listed Markdown/MDX references to the new per-step captures.
4. Optimize the image, run `npm start`, visit the target documentation page, and verify every image renders and matches the adjacent text.
5. Commit with `docs(screenshots): refresh <area> per issue #<N>` and open a PR for the child issue.

### Audit findings and assigned children

#### Exact duplicate asset groups

The following MD5-equal groups must become concept-specific captures through their assigned children:

| Duplicate group | Paths | Child |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 9 product limitation tabs | `static/img/config/product-{custom-domains,disk-space,hide-credits,plugins,post-types,reset-limitations,site-templates,themes,upgrades}.png` (28,236 B each) | #69 |
| 7 dashboard views | `static/img/admin/network-dashboard-{activity-stream,first-steps,full,news,right-now,summary}.png`, `static/img/installation/network-dashboard.png` (125,540 B each) | #70 |
| 3 payment settings shots | `static/img/admin/settings-payments-{bottom,gateways-2,options}.png` | #71 |
| 2 period-selection views | `static/img/config/period-selection-field-{options,settings}.png` | #72 |
| 2 installation shots | `static/img/installation/plugin-activated.png`, `static/img/installation/wizard-welcome.png` | #75 |
| 2 dashboard shots | `static/img/admin/um-dashboard-bottom.png`, `static/img/admin/um-dashboard-stats.png` | #76 |

#### Placeholder walkthroughs already covered

- #65: `docs/user-guide/integrations/zapier.md` has 14 distinct Zapier concepts but uses `webhooks-list.png`; it needs the dashboard, app search, trigger picker, auth, Ultimate Multisite API settings, credentials, `payment_received`, test step, action setup, and the other described steps.
- #66: `docs/user-guide/payment-gateways/stripe.md` has 13 concepts but repeatedly uses `settings-payment-gateways.png`; cover active gateways, inline card, Checkout redirect, keys, Stripe dashboard, test data, webhooks, listener URL, and endpoint setup.
- #67: `docs/user-guide/payment-gateways/paypal.md` has 5 concepts but reuses the payment settings image for PayPal-side steps.
- #68: `docs/user-guide/client-management/account-page.md` has 16 customer-facing account concepts but reuses network-admin images. Cover account menu/overview, plan, limits, billing, profile update, template switching, domain/DNS flow, password, and Danger Zone.
- #74: replace the heavy `/img/admin/webhooks-list.png` placeholder reuse in the Zapier registration/webhook flow.

#### High-reuse images and the corresponding program work

`/img/admin/webhooks-list.png` is referenced 35 times (#65, #74); `/img/config/settings-payment-gateways.png` 34 times (#66, #67); `/img/admin/memberships-list.png` 17 times; `/img/config/checkout-form-step.png` 16 times (#72, #73); `/img/config/settings-taxes.png` 15 times; and `/img/config/discount-codes-list.png` 14 times. The last four are resolved by the child issues below or future focused work, not by a blanket asset replacement.

### Gap-page children from the second audit

Use these exact page-level findings when executing #86–#96. The line references were recorded on the audit revision; verify current context before editing.

| Child | Documentation file | Required distinct captures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #86 | `docs/user-guide/payment-gateways/getting-paid.md` | Replace 18 placeholders: `settings-payment-gateways.png` at L16,22,26,30,34,36,42 for payment rows/toggles/invoice settings, and `settings-general.png` at L62,66,70,74,78,86,90,94,102,106,110 for WooCommerce, GoCardless, and Payfast install dialogs. |
| #87 | `docs/user-guide/payment-gateways/manual-payments.md` | Replace three `settings-payment-gateways.png` uses (manual toggle, frontend instructions, Thank You page) and three `payments-list.png` uses (list, detail, status change/activate-membership). Check reusable orphans before recapture. |
| #88 | `docs/user-guide/payment-gateways/tax-handling.md` | Replace 15 `settings-taxes.png` uses (L18,26,38,42,52,54,58,60,80,84,86,90,94,102,110): tax toggles/rates/categories, VAT add-on install and activation, VAT support, EU rate pull, and frontend VAT field. |
| #89 | `docs/user-guide/configuration/creating-discount-codes.md` | Replace 14 `discount-codes-list.png` uses (L16,22,24,28,36,40,44,50,54,64,66,70,74,78). First assess and wire accurate orphan assets `discount-code-edit.png`, `discount-code-active.png`, `discount-code-advanced.png`, `discount-code-description.png`, `discount-code-save.png`, and `discount-codes-empty.png`. |
| #90 | `docs/user-guide/configuration/the-registration-flow.md` | Replace 9 uses across `checkout-forms-list.png` (L20), `checkout-form-editor.png` (L26,32), `settings-payment-gateways.png` (L46,50,54), and `payments-list.png` (L60,64,66,70); include customer registration, Thank You page, activation, manual payment, and admin payment processing. |
| #91 | `docs/user-guide/client-management/upgrading-a-plan.md` | Replace 5 `memberships-list.png` placeholders (customer account, membership change, plan checkout, upgrade summary, no-change state) and 3 `product-upgrades.png` placeholders (admin up/downgrades and plan-group assignment). |
| #92 | `docs/user-guide/client-management/canceling-a-membership.md` | Replace 6 `memberships-list.png` usages (L16,20,24,26,30; two images on L30) with customer Danger Zone, confirmation, logged-out, cancellation, and retained-customer states. |
| #93 | `docs/user-guide/client-management/downgrading-a-plan.md` | Replace 3 `memberships-list.png` shots (change control, plans, pending-change) and `settings-sites.png` (post-limit options). |
| #94 | `docs/user-guide/client-management/client-websites.md` | Replace 6 `customers-list.png` shots (L12,18,22,26,30,34) with customer My Sites, account menu, default-site selection, dropdown, and confirmation. |
| #95 | `docs/user-guide/domain-mapping/how-to-configure-domain-mapping.md` | Replace 7 `settings-domain-mapping.png` and 9 `domains-list.png` placeholders: sunrise wizard, mapping controls, redirects/user access, product custom-domain choice, integration/hosting, domains list/add modal/transitions/detail, and subsite controls. |
| #96 | `docs/user-guide/miscellaneous/sending-emails-and-broadcasts.md` | Replace 9 `broadcasts-list.png` uses (customer notice, menu, add modal as message/email, targeting, editor) and 5 `settings-emails.png` uses (Emails settings, customization, reset/import/options). |

### Additional program scope and decisions

- #84 owns the 28 addon index pages with no screenshots.
- #85 owns the 48 orphan static images; use accurate existing images before creating replacements, particularly for #89, #95, and #87.
- Future focused issues may cover VAT/tax, discount codes, domain mapping, WooCommerce, GoCardless, PayFast, Language Selector, Site Exporter, Admin Page Creator, and administration-tour refreshes when not already covered above.
- Do not reopen #78 (duplicate master), #79 (covered by #65/#74), #80 (covered by #66/#67/#71 and #86–#88), #81 (covered by #69/#72/#73/#77 and #89/#90), #82 (covered by #68 and #91–#94), or #83 (covered by #95/#96 plus the future list-state refresh).

### Audit reproducibility

Use the following checks when reassessing a target area:

```bash
git ls-files | grep -iE '\.(png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp)$'
find static/img -type f -name '*.png' -exec md5sum {} \; | sort | uniq -d -w 32
grep -rohE '/img/[^)" ]+\.png' docs/ | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
find static/img -name '*.png' -exec file {} \;
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each child issue has an accurate, per-concept capture plan; no implementation PR reuses a known placeholder image for a materially different UI state.
- [ ] New/replaced screenshots meet the capture standards, optimize their PNGs, and render correctly in the relevant documentation page.
- [ ] The duplicate groups and per-page placeholder work are completed only through their focused child issues, with #85 assessed before recapturing candidate orphan assets.
- [ ] The screenshot program retains the documented child-issue coverage and does not reopen superseded duplicate programs #78–#83.
- [ ] The two populated-list refresh pages remain explicitly deferred until separately filed.

## Context & Decisions

- **Original audit / #64:** established the asset counts, duplicate groups, capture standards, child #65–#77 queue, and original future-work candidates. Its core decision was one focused issue per screenshot area rather than a monolithic asset change.
- **@superdav42, Comment 1:** reported a parallel duplicate audit (#78/#79/#80), added the zero-screenshot addon and orphan-file categories, and recommended retaining the #64 program with focused children rather than parallel section trackers.
- **@superdav42, Comment 2:** reconciled the two methodologies, recorded 11 additional placeholder-reuse pages and two data-state pages, retained #84/#85 as net-new issues, and confirmed #78–#83 were duplicates.
- **@superdav42, Comment 3:** confirmed that the 11 gap pages were filed as #86–#96 and supplied the complete index tying every affected page to its focused child. This supersedes the earlier proposal to create those children.
- **Final agreed approach:** this single issue is the program specification; execute focused children, reuse accurate orphan assets where possible, and keep capture operations reproducible and optimized.

## Contributors

cc @superdav42

## Files Scope

**Hard boundaries:** This is a coordination tracker. It authorizes no direct repository-file changes; source and asset edits belong only to the explicitly linked child issues.

**AI brief owner:** Pulse consolidation workflow.

title: Docs update: Ultimate Multisite v2.18.0
body:
## Release

Ultimate Multisite v2.18.0 — release dated 2026-10-27. Publication follows the core plugin's GitHub and WordPress.org workflow, not the addon WooCommerce workflow.

## Required doc updates

- [ ] `docs/user-guide/host-integrations/bigscoots.md` (new page) — document BigScoots setup and automatic domain mapping. Follow the existing GridPane host integration guide. Source: `inc/integrations/providers/bigscoots/` in the core plugin.
- [ ] `docs/user-guide/configuration/checkout-forms.md` — document opt-in provisioning progress, host-history ETA, signed site handoff, and legacy-flow defaults. Verify options against core checkout and `inc/provisioning/`; do not imply every form enables these features automatically.
- [ ] `docs/user-guide/administration/managing-system-emails.md` — explain delayed scheduling, product targeting, trial-expiring events, and the per-email network-name subject prefix. Sources: core `inc/admin-pages/class-email-edit-admin-page.php`, `inc/managers/class-email-manager.php`, and `inc/models/class-email.php`.
- [ ] `docs/user-guide/administration/managing-payments-and-invoices.md` — describe supported invoice writing systems, bundled fonts, Arabic/CJK handling, font selection, and errors for unsupported scripts. Sources: core `inc/invoices/` and the invoice font assets; list only scripts actually shipped.
- [ ] `docs/developer/addon-development/getting-started.md` — add a practical add-on catalog extension example, following core `inc/class-addon-repository.php` and the catalog extension points introduced in core PR #1941. Hook references are generated; do not hand-edit those pages.
- [ ] `docs/developer/integration-guide/index.md` — explain custom provisioning pipelines and progress reporting using core `inc/functions/provisioning.php` and `inc/provisioning/class-provisioning-progress.php`; document signed handoff integration only after verifying its current contract.
- [ ] `docs/user-guide/domain-mapping/how-to-configure-domain-mapping.md` — explain permanent HTTP 301 primary-domain redirects, read-only DNS lookup diagnostics, and displayed nameservers. Cross-reference the generated `wu_domain_mapping_fallback` hook rather than manually editing its generated reference.

## Documentation assessment

Manual updates are required for all five New changelog entries (hosting, checkout/handoff, system emails, invoice fonts, and developer extensions). Delayed-email behavior, redirect defaults, and DNS UI guidance also need the updates above. The remaining fixes preserve intended behavior; editor/statistics performance, source asset freshness, dependency updates, and internal verification do not need manual pages. No new REST endpoint is claimed without source verification. Generated hook references and changelogs remain owned by the documentation generation pipeline.

## Verification

Check every option and API example against the v2.18.0 core source. Build the docs with the repository's existing documented build command, verify links/sidebar reachability, and ensure generated hooks/changelogs are not hand-edited. The paths above were discovered from the docs repository tree; BigScoots is explicitly a new page. Do not invent other paths if additional pages are needed: discover them first.

## Changelog entry

```text
Version [2.18.0] - Released on 2026-10-27
- New: BigScoots hosting integration supports automatic domain mapping.
- New: Checkout can show step-by-step site provisioning progress with estimated completion times and a signed handoff to the new site.
- New: System emails support product targeting, a trial-expiring event, and an optional network-name subject prefix.
- New: Invoice PDFs include bundled fonts for more languages and writing systems.
- New: Developers can extend the add-on catalog and customize fallback domain lookup.
- Fix: Stripe checkout handles multi-step forms, free recurring plans, cart currencies, discounts, trials, and initial payment expiration more reliably.
- Fix: Outstanding invoices on active memberships and refunds with fractional discount totals now work correctly.
- Fix: Paid checkout publishes pending sites reliably, customer panels isolate pending sites, and orphaned pending sites can be deleted safely.
- Fix: Bulk site deletion no longer risks deleting unrelated sites whose IDs match pending memberships.
- Fix: Secondary networks initialize their tables reliably and use the correct network's metadata, limits, pending sites, and model events.
```
